2.title: Dictatorships of the 20th Century II
2.text: Kamila Staudigl-Ciechowicz — the Austrian case, from the elimination of parliament to the Anschluss and Nuremberg.

3.title: National Socialism in Austria before 1938
3.text: Small parties calling themselves National Socialist had existed in Austria since 1918, allied with the German National Socialists from around 1925 but WITHOUT POLITICAL SIGNIFICANCE. Electoral success in Germany brings an upswing in Austria too: entry into the provincial parliaments of VIENNA, LOWER AUSTRIA AND SALZBURG and into the FEDERAL COUNCIL in 1931/32. And the lecture's assessment: THE NATIONAL COUNCIL ELECTIONS SCHEDULED FOR 1934 WOULD CERTAINLY HAVE RESULTED IN A RESOUNDING VICTORY FOR THE NATIONAL SOCIALISTS. Keep that in mind when judging what the government did in March 1933 — it was avoiding an election it expected to lose.

cards.q: What was the expected outcome of the Austrian National Council elections scheduled for 1934?
cards.a: A resounding victory for the National Socialists, who had entered the provincial parliaments of Vienna, Lower Austria and Salzburg and the Federal Council in 1931/32. The elimination of parliament in March 1933 avoided an election the government expected to lose.

4.title: The elimination of the National Council, March 1933
4.text: The 1930 elections made the SdAP the strongest party, and it supplied the President of the National Council, KARL RENNER — but the government stayed with the Christian Socials and two other bourgeois or right-wing parties, with ENGELBERT DOLLFUSS as Federal Chancellor from 1932. On 4 MARCH 1933 ALL THREE NATIONAL COUNCIL PRESIDENTS RESIGN FOR A TRIVIAL REASON, over a disputed vote — and the RULES OF PROCEDURE CONTAIN NO PROVISION FOR THIS CASE, so nobody can convene the chamber. Dollfuss is SURPRISED by this development BUT USES IT to eliminate parliament, calling it the ALLEGED 'SELF-EXCLUSION OF PARLIAMENT'. On 15 March POLICE PREVENT PARLIAMENT FROM RECONVENING. A gap in the standing orders turned into the end of parliamentary government.

terms.def: Dollfuss's description of the accident of 4 March 1933, when all three presidents of the National Council resigned and the rules of procedure provided no way to reconvene it.

cards.q: How was the Austrian National Council eliminated in March 1933?
cards.a: On 4 March all three of its presidents resigned over a trivial dispute, and the rules of procedure contained no provision for that case, so nobody could convene the chamber. Dollfuss, surprised, used it — calling it the 'self-exclusion of parliament' — and on 15 March police prevented parliament from reconvening.

5.title: Governing on a wartime statute — and removing the court
5.text: The government rules authoritatively and relies on the WARTIME ECONOMY ENABLING ACT OF 1917, whose § 1 authorises the government, DURING THE PERIOD OF EXTRAORDINARY CONDITIONS CAUSED BY THE WAR, to make by decree the dispositions necessary to promote economic life, prevent economic damage and supply the population with food and commodities. It authorises WAR ECONOMY MEASURES — food rationing — AND IS NOW BEING MISUSED. On that basis come CENSORSHIP, restrictions on freedom of assembly, and bans on the Communists and the National Socialists. And then the decisive step: when the Social Democrats try to have the emergency ordinances REVIEWED BY THE CONSTITUTIONAL COURT, THE GOVERNMENT USES AN EMERGENCY ORDINANCE TO ELIMINATE THE CONSTITUTIONAL COURT. The Viennese phrase on the slide says it: 'we won't need a judge'.

cards.q: On what legal basis did the Dollfuss government rule after March 1933, and why was that a misuse?
cards.a: On the Wartime Economy Enabling Act of 1917, which authorised the government to act by decree only for war-economy purposes during the extraordinary conditions caused by the war — food supply, prevention of economic damage. It was used instead for censorship, restrictions on assembly and party bans, fifteen years after the war.

cards.q: What happened when the Social Democrats challenged the emergency ordinances?
cards.a: The government used an emergency ordinance to ELIMINATE THE CONSTITUTIONAL COURT — removing the institution that was about to review its own legality.

7.title: One party and a new constitution
7.text: 12 FEBRUARY 1934: the Social Democratic Party is BANNED. By autumn 1934 all still existing parties DISSOLVE THEMSELVES, the Christian Socials among them. 21 MAY 1933: the FATHERLAND FRONT is founded — 'bearer of the Austrian state idea' — now the single party. 30 APRIL 1934: the National Council convenes FOR THE LAST TIME, WITHOUT THE SOCIAL DEMOCRATIC DEPUTIES — a RUMP PARLIAMENT — and approves the new constitution ALREADY ADOPTED BY THE GOVERNMENT, giving the government UNLIMITED LEGISLATIVE POWERS INCLUDING CONSTITUTIONAL LEGISLATION. Note the order: the government adopts the constitution first, and the rump parliament ratifies it afterwards.

terms.def: The Fatherland Front, founded 21 May 1933 as 'bearer of the Austrian state idea' — the single party of the corporative state.

cards.q: What did the National Council do at its last sitting on 30 April 1934?
cards.a: Meeting as a rump parliament without the banned Social Democrats, it approved the new constitution ALREADY ADOPTED BY THE GOVERNMENT and gave the government unlimited legislative powers, including constitutional legislation.

8.title: Where the corporative state came from
8.text: In 1931 POPE PIUS XI proposes the revival of CORPORATIVE STRUCTURES — Stände — in order to OVERCOME THE MARXIST CLASS STRUGGLE, in the encyclical QUADRAGESIMO ANNO. In 1933 Dollfuss promises to establish a CORPORATIVE STATE, in which — his example — farmers and farm labourers form a COMMON estate. The idea is to replace the division between classes with a division by occupation, so that employer and employee sit in the same body.

terms.def: A state organised by occupational estates rather than parties, meant to overcome class struggle by putting employers and employees in one body. Proposed by Pius XI in Quadragesimo anno (1931).

cards.q: Where does the idea of the corporative state come from, and what is it meant to achieve?
cards.a: From the encyclical Quadragesimo anno of Pope Pius XI (1931), reviving corporative structures — Stände — in order to overcome the Marxist class struggle: employers and employees, such as farmers and farm labourers, belong to a common estate instead of opposing classes.

9.title: Austrofascism? The balance sheet
9.text: The 1934 constitution provides that the VOCATIONAL GROUPS should take part in legislation — but IN CONSTITUTIONAL REALITY THESE PROVISIONS CANNOT BE IMPLEMENTED UNTIL 1938, and the legislative power of the federal government dominates: a CHANCELLOR DICTATORSHIP. And then the balance sheet the exam likes, each item with its counterweight. The constitution COMMITS TO THE SEPARATION OF POWERS — but THE INDEPENDENCE OF JUDGES IS ELIMINATED. It CONTAINS FUNDAMENTAL RIGHTS — but with restrictions such as censorship and no equality of men and women. It provides CONSTITUTIONAL JUSTICE — in reality MEANINGLESS. There are NO ANTI-SEMITIC LAWS AND NO CONCENTRATION CAMPS — but widespread antisemitism in the population, AS EVERYWHERE IN EUROPE. Its policy is ANTI-NATIONALIST — but AGAINST DEMOCRACY AND AGAINST MARXISM. Whether to call it fascism is the question the slide leaves open, and an answer should use both columns.

cards.q: Set out the balance sheet on whether the Austrian corporative state was 'austrofascism'.
cards.a: For each promise a counterweight: it committed to the separation of powers but eliminated judicial independence; it contained fundamental rights but with censorship and no equality of the sexes; it provided constitutional justice that was meaningless in reality; it had no anti-Semitic laws and no concentration camps, but widespread popular antisemitism as elsewhere in Europe; and its policy was anti-nationalist but also anti-democratic and anti-Marxist.

cards.q: Why is the 1934 regime called a 'chancellor dictatorship'?
cards.a: Because the corporative provisions on participation of the vocational groups in legislation could not be implemented before 1938, so in constitutional reality the legislative power of the federal government — and of the chancellor — dominated.

10.title: Dollfuss against the Anschluss, and the Rome Protocols
10.text: By 1933 the MAJORITY OF THE POPULATION WANTED THE ANSCHLUSS to the German Reich — and there is A FUNDAMENTAL CHANGE AFTER HITLER'S RISE TO POWER. Dollfuss takes a firm stand AGAINST the Anschluss and BANS THE NSDAP; Germany reacts with the THOUSAND-MARK BAN, crippling Austrian tourism. Mussolini concludes the ROME PROTOCOLS with Austria and Hungary in 1934 and assures both of his support. Meanwhile Nazis carry out ACTS OF TERRORISM in Austria with numerous deaths. Note the irony that runs through the next slides: Austrian independence in 1934 rests on MUSSOLINI.

cards.q: How did Austrian opinion on the Anschluss change, and on whom did Austrian independence then rest?
cards.a: Until 1933 a majority wanted the Anschluss; Hitler's rise to power changed that fundamentally. Dollfuss opposed it and banned the NSDAP; Germany retaliated with the Thousand-Mark Ban. Austrian independence then rested on MUSSOLINI, through the Rome Protocols of 1934 with Italy and Hungary.

11.title: The Nazi coup attempt, 25 July 1934
11.text: Nazis occupy the FEDERAL CHANCELLERY and the BROADCASTING BUILDING. The members of the government escape; DOLLFUSS HIMSELF IS SHOT AND BLEEDS TO DEATH. MUSSOLINI DEPLOYS TROOPS AT THE AUSTRO-ITALIAN BORDER to prevent Hitler's imminent intervention, and the coup collapses — well over 200 dead. KURT SCHUSCHNIGG becomes the new Federal Chancellor and continues Dollfuss's policies by and large.

cards.q: What happened on 25 July 1934, and what stopped it?
cards.a: Austrian Nazis occupied the Federal Chancellery and the broadcasting building; Dollfuss was shot and bled to death. Mussolini deployed troops on the Austro-Italian border to deter Hitler's intervention, and the coup collapsed with well over 200 dead. Schuschnigg became chancellor.

12.title: The Berlin–Rome axis and the road to March 1938
12.text: The ITALO-ABYSSINIAN WAR of 1935–1937 leaves Mussolini isolated and pushes Italy towards Germany — SO AUSTRIA IS ON ITS OWN. In 1936 it has to make major concessions: an AMNESTY FOR NATIONAL SOCIALISTS and TWO NATIONAL SOCIALIST MEMBERS IN THE GOVERNMENT. On 12 FEBRUARY 1938, in talks with Schuschnigg, Hitler FORCES THE APPOINTMENT OF THE NAZI ARTHUR SEYSS-INQUART AS MINISTER OF THE INTERIOR — the ministry that controls the police. Schuschnigg then seeks the support of the population and ANNOUNCES A REFERENDUM FOR AN INDEPENDENT AUSTRIA ON 13 MARCH.

cards.q: Why was Austria left on its own by 1936, and what did that cost it?
cards.a: The Italo-Abyssinian war of 1935–1937 isolated Mussolini and drove Italy towards Germany, so Austria lost its protector. It had to concede an amnesty for National Socialists and two National Socialist ministers in 1936, and in February 1938 Hitler forced the appointment of Seyss-Inquart as Minister of the Interior.

13.title: The Anschluss, and how it was made legal
13.text: 11 MARCH: Hitler forces Schuschnigg's resignation and SEYSS-INQUART becomes Federal Chancellor. 12 MARCH: German troops march into Austria. 13 MARCH: Federal President Miklas resigns and SEYSS-INQUART ALSO TAKES OVER HIS FUNCTIONS — IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE 1934 CONSTITUTION. And then the part that belongs in a legal history lecture: the Anschluss is established by TWO LITERALLY IDENTICAL LAWS. The AUSTRIAN Anschluss Act, enacted by the Austrian federal government under Seyss-Inquart ON THE BASIS OF THE AUSTRIAN ENABLING ACT OF 1934; and the GERMAN Anschluss Act, enacted by the German Reich government under Hitler ON THE BASIS OF THE GERMAN ENABLING ACT OF 1933. Each dictatorship used its own enabling act — the Austrian corporative state's instrument was the means by which Austria abolished itself.

cards.q: By which legal instruments was the Anschluss carried out?
cards.a: By two LITERALLY IDENTICAL laws: the Austrian Anschluss Act, enacted by Seyss-Inquart's federal government on the basis of the Austrian Enabling Act of 1934, and the German Anschluss Act, enacted by Hitler's government on the basis of the German Enabling Act of 1933.

cards.q: Trace the three days of March 1938.
cards.a: 11 March: Hitler forces Schuschnigg's resignation and Seyss-Inquart becomes chancellor. 12 March: German troops march in. 13 March: President Miklas resigns and Seyss-Inquart takes over his functions as well — in accordance with the 1934 constitution.

14.title: The legal consequences
14.text: Austria becomes A 'LAND' OF THE GERMAN REICH, like Bavaria — the division into seven Reich districts comes only in 1940. AUSTRIAN LAW REMAINS IN FORCE, the ABGB included, AND EVEN PARTS OF CONSTITUTIONAL LAW — BUT NO FUNDAMENTAL RIGHTS AND NO CONSTITUTIONAL JURISDICTION. And a referendum is held ON 10 APRIL — that is, RETROSPECTIVELY, four weeks after the event it was supposed to decide.

cards.q: What happened to Austrian law after the Anschluss?
cards.a: It remained in force — the ABGB included, and even parts of constitutional law — BUT without fundamental rights and without constitutional jurisdiction. Austria became a 'Land' of the German Reich, divided into seven Reich districts only in 1940.

cards.q: When was the Anschluss referendum held, and why is the date significant?
cards.a: On 10 April 1938 — RETROSPECTIVELY, four weeks after the Anschluss of 13 March. The vote did not decide the question; it ratified what had already happened.

15.title: The ballot paper
15.text: The question put on 10 April: 'DO YOU AGREE WITH THE REUNIFICATION OF AUSTRIA WITH THE GERMAN REICH, WHICH TOOK PLACE ON 13 MARCH 1938, AND DO YOU VOTE FOR THE LIST OF OUR FÜHRER ADOLF HITLER?' Yes or No. Read what is being done: the accomplished fact is described as a reunification, TWO QUESTIONS ARE FUSED INTO ONE so that a vote on the Anschluss is also a vote for the list, and the Yes circle on the printed ballot is larger than the No.

cards.q: What is wrong with the ballot question of 10 April 1938, considered as a vote?
cards.a: It asks about an accomplished fact, describes it as a 'reunification', and FUSES TWO QUESTIONS — approval of the Anschluss and a vote for Hitler's list — into a single Yes or No, so neither can be answered separately.

16.title: The Munich Agreement, 1938
16.text: SIX LANGUAGES are spoken in Czechoslovakia: Czech, German, Slovak, Hungarian, Ukrainian and Polish. On 29 SEPTEMBER 1938 Germany, Italy, the UK and France agree that Czechoslovakia MUST HAND OVER the German-, Hungarian- and Polish-speaking territories to the respective neighbouring states — and A GUARANTEE OF CONTINUED EXISTENCE IS GIVEN FOR THE REST. On 14/15 MARCH 1939 Hitler annexes the Czech territories and Horthy the Ukrainian ones, and SLOVAKIA BECOMES A FORMALLY INDEPENDENT STATE, de facto dependent on Hitler. The guarantee lasted under six months. Note the mechanism: self-determination by language, applied by four powers to a fifth state, with the affected state not present.

cards.q: What did the Munich Agreement decide, and what happened to its guarantee?
cards.a: On 29 September 1938 Germany, Italy, the UK and France agreed that Czechoslovakia must hand its German-, Hungarian- and Polish-speaking territories to the neighbouring states, with a guarantee of continued existence for the rest. On 14/15 March 1939 Hitler annexed the Czech lands, Horthy the Ukrainian ones, and Slovakia became formally independent — the guarantee had lasted under six months.

17.title: The attack on Poland, 1939
17.text: Hitler and Stalin conclude a NON-AGGRESSION PACT in August 1939 and DIVIDE EAST-CENTRAL EUROPE INTO 'ZONES OF INTEREST'. Hitler's invasion of Poland leads the UK and France to declare war on Germany — the Second World War. The cartoon on the slide catches it: Hitler and Stalin greeting each other over the body of Poland — 'the scum of the earth, I believe?' — 'the bloody assassin of the workers, I presume?'

cards.q: What did the Hitler–Stalin pact of August 1939 contain beyond non-aggression?
cards.a: A division of east-central Europe into 'zones of interest' between the two powers. Hitler's invasion of Poland then brought British and French declarations of war — the Second World War.

18.title: The Nuremberg Trials, 1945/46
18.text: TWO MAIN LEGAL ISSUES, and they are the point of the slide for a legal historian. INDIVIDUAL RESPONSIBILITY IN INTERNATIONAL LAW — international law had bound states, not persons. And the RETROACTIVE FORCE OF CRIMINAL LAWS — nullum crimen sine lege, the very principle the late Qing and every modern code insists on. THE CHARGES: CRIMES AGAINST PEACE; WAR CRIMES IN THE NARROWER SENSE; and CRIMES AGAINST HUMANITY. IN THE DOCK: Göring, Hess, Ribbentrop, SEYSS-INQUART, von Schirach and others. Dead by suicide before the trial: Hitler, Goebbels, Himmler. The trial had to answer both objections before it could try anyone — which is why Nuremberg belongs to legal history and not only to the history of the war.

terms.def: One of the three Nuremberg charges, beside crimes against peace and war crimes in the narrower sense — and the one that required both individual responsibility in international law and an answer to the objection of retroactivity.

cards.q: What were the two main legal problems of the Nuremberg trials?
cards.a: Whether international law knows INDIVIDUAL responsibility — it had bound states, not persons — and whether criminal laws could be applied RETROACTIVELY, against nullum crimen sine lege.

cards.q: Name the three Nuremberg charges, and one Austrian defendant.
cards.a: Crimes against peace, war crimes in the narrower sense, and crimes against humanity. Among the defendants was Arthur Seyss-Inquart — the man who had signed the Austrian Anschluss Act — beside Göring, Hess, Ribbentrop and von Schirach.
